read.sections.0.heading.source: Many AI tools learn from examples
read.sections.0.heading.back: Many AI tools learn from examples

read.sections.0.text.source: AI stands for artificial intelligence. Artificial means made by people. AI is a big field with many methods. Many AI systems used today learn patterns from data, and this lesson is about them. People give the program a lot of data, such as photos, sentences or voice recordings. The program looks for a pattern in the data. Then it uses that pattern to make a prediction. A prediction is a careful guess about something new, based on the patterns, not a random one. At Hillview Learning Centre, the translation tool learned from many sentences in two languages. When you type a sentence it has never seen, it predicts a good translation.
read.sections.0.text.back: AI is short for artificial intelligence, that is, "kecerdasan buatan". "Buatan" means made by people. AI is a big field with many methods. Many AI systems used today learn patterns from data, and this lesson is about those systems. People give the program a lot of data, such as photos, sentences or voice recordings. The program looks for patterns in the data. Then it uses the pattern to make a prediction. A prediction is a careful guess about something new, based on patterns, not a random guess. At Hillview Learning Centre, the translation tool learned from many sentences in two languages. When you type a sentence it has never seen, it predicts a good translation.
read.sections.0.text.note: The standard text keeps the English words "artificial intelligence" once, so learners see where the letters AI come from; "AI" stays AI throughout the course. "Careful guess" is "tekaan yang teliti" everywhere in Digital World.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: AI means artificial intelligence. People make it. There are many kinds of AI. Many AI programs today learn from examples. This lesson is about them. People give a program lots of data, like photos or voices. It finds a pattern in the data. Then it makes a prediction. This is a careful guess about something new. It is not random. The Hillview translation tool learned from many sentences. It can guess how to translate a new one.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: AI means artificial intelligence. People make it. There are many kinds of AI. Many AI programs today learn from examples. This lesson is about those programs. People give it a lot of data, such as photos or voices. It looks for patterns in the data. Then it makes a prediction. This is a careful guess about something new. It is not a random guess. The Hillview translation tool learned from many sentences. It can guess the translation of a new sentence.

read.sections.1.text.source: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows fixed steps that a person wrote, for sums with one right answer. It always gives 12 for 7 + 5, and it never learned that from examples. The bell at Hillview rings at nine o'clock because someone set a timer. The AI tools in this lesson are different, because they must estimate. A new voice or photo is never exactly like their examples. Still, following rules does not prove a tool is not AI. Some AI follows rules that people wrote, and some mixes rules and learning. A fan called “smart” might follow one simple rule, or it might learn. Sometimes the honest answer is “hard to say”.
read.sections.1.text.back: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows fixed steps written by someone, for sums that have only one right answer. It always gives 12 for 7 + 5, and it never learned that from examples. The bell at Hillview rings at nine o'clock because someone set a timer. The AI tools in this lesson are different, because they must estimate. A new voice or photo is never completely the same as their examples. However, following rules does not prove a tool is not AI. Some AI follows rules written by people, and some combine rules with learning. A fan called “smart” may follow one simple rule, or it may learn. Sometimes the honest answer is “hard to say”.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows steps a person wrote. It always says 7 + 5 is 12. It did not learn this. The Hillview bell rings at nine. Someone set a timer. The AI tools here must make a careful guess. A new photo is never the same as their examples. But some AI follows rules that people wrote. Some uses rules and examples. So it can be hard to tell. A “smart” fan may follow one rule, or it may learn.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows steps written by someone. It always says 7 + 5 is 12. It did not learn this. The Hillview bell rings at nine o'clock. Someone set a timer. The AI tools here must make a careful guess. A new photo is never the same as their examples. But some AI follows rules written by people. Some use rules and examples. So sometimes it is hard to know. A “smart” fan may follow one rule, or it may learn.

read.sections.2.heading.source: AI is a tool, not a person
read.sections.2.heading.back: AI is a tool, not a person

read.sections.2.text.source: AI can seem clever, but it does not think or feel like a person. It does not understand a photo or a sentence the way you do. It finds patterns in data and makes a guess. That guess can be wrong, especially when something is new or very different from its examples. People decide what an AI tool is for, what data it learns from and when to trust its answers. So you can ask three questions about any AI tool. What does it guess? What examples did it learn from? Who checks if it is right?
read.sections.2.text.back: AI can look clever, but it does not think or feel like a person. It does not understand a photo or a sentence the way you understand it. It looks for patterns in data and makes a guess. That guess can be mistaken, especially when something is new or very different from its examples. People decide what an AI tool is for, what data it learns and when its answers can be trusted. So you can ask three questions about any AI tool. What does it guess? What examples did it learn? Who checks whether it is right?
read.sections.2.text.note: "Can be wrong" is "boleh tersilap" (can be mistaken), softer than "salah", which the house style avoids.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: AI can seem clever. But it does not think or feel like a person. It finds patterns and makes a guess. The guess can be wrong, more often when something is new. People choose what AI is for, its data and when to trust it. Ask three questions. What does it guess? What did it learn from? Who checks it?
read.sections.2.simpler.back: AI can look clever. But it does not think or feel like a person. It looks for patterns and makes a guess. The guess can be mistaken, especially when something is new. write.example.source: I chose the voice typing tool. I think it uses AI because it has to make a careful guess at the words from each new voice. It learned from lots of voice recordings and found patterns in them. One mistake it could make is typing the wrong word when someone speaks fast or quietly. A person should check the typed words before using them. The calculator is different. It follows steps a person wrote, and it does not learn from examples.
write.example.back: I chose the tool for typing with your voice. I think it uses AI because it has to make a careful guess about the words from each new voice. It learned from many voice recordings and looked for patterns in them. One mistake it might make is typing a word that is not right when someone speaks fast or in a voice that is too quiet. Someone needs to check the typed words before using them. The calculator, though, is different. It follows steps written by someone, and it does not learn from examples.

watch.summary.source: In this short video, two people who work with AI talk about machine learning. AI is already part of everyday life. It helps choose what people see online, for example when they search. Many people imagine AI as a robot that thinks like a person. The speakers say that kind of AI is still many years away. Most AI today is machine learning. In the past, people had to write every step for a computer. With machine learning, people give the computer lots of examples. The computer finds patterns in the examples by itself. This is a bit like how you learn from practice. It is a new way to get computers to do useful jobs.
watch.summary.back: In this short video, two people who work with AI talk about machine learning. AI is already part of daily life. It helps choose what people see online, for example when they search. Many people imagine AI as a robot that thinks like a person. Both speakers say that kind of AI is still years away. Most AI today is machine learning. In the past, people had to write every step for the computer. With machine learning, people give the computer many examples. The computer looks for patterns in those examples by itself. This is a little like how you learn through practice. This is a new way to make computers do useful work.

educatorNotes.0.source: There is no single agreed line between AI and other programs (see the OECD source). AI is a broad field: Stanford HAI calls it computer systems that do tasks with human-like intelligence, and says modern AI often works by finding patterns in data. This lesson introduces that common modern kind (machine learning); rule-based AI, such as the expert systems in Lesson 2, is AI too. Accept “hard to say” and reward reasons, not the group a learner picks. The activity has no score.
educatorNotes.0.back: There is no single agreed dividing line between AI and other programs (see the OECD source). AI is a broad field: Stanford HAI calls it computer systems that do tasks with human-like intelligence, and says modern AI often works by looking for patterns in data. This lesson introduces that common modern kind (machine learning); rule-based AI, like the expert systems in Lesson 2, is also AI. Accept “hard to say” answers and value the reasons given, not the group the learner chooses. This activity has no marks.
